LANDED as 9b764d518 (Gerrit change 1004, LLM-Review +1 / Verified +1, MERGED).

WHAT SHIPPED
- scripts/check_commit_message_wrap.py — check-only 50/72 checker (never rewrites a message; names the offending lines).
- .pre-commit-config.yaml — `commit-message-wrap` hook at the commit-msg stage + top-level `default_install_hook_types: [pre-commit, commit-msg]`.
- Makefile — `make hooks` verifies both hook types and the Change-Id chain.
- CONTRIBUTING.md — enforcement, exemption list, commit-msg-stage rationale, never-run-`-f` warning.
- tests/unit/test_check_commit_message_wrap.py — 20 tests.

AC-BY-AC EVIDENCE

AC "over-72 body line REJECTED, naming each line": verified by REJECTING MY OWN COMMIT. First attempt output:
    - line 7 is 73 chars (limit 72): 'nothing here checked it: bodies on main range from 72 to'…
    - line 8 is 73 chars (limit 72): …  - line 9 is 73 chars … - line 32 is 73 chars …
AC "subject over 50 REJECTED": second attempt output:
    - subject is 58 chars (limit 50): '514d: enforce the 50/72 commit-message rule at commit time'…
Third attempt passed the gate ("commit message (50/72 wrap; never mutates)...Passed") and committed. The landed commit's max body line length is exactly 72.

AC "conforming commit still receives Change-Id (Gerrit hook chained, not clobbered)": the landed commit carries all three trailers —
    rebar-ticket: 514d-3aac-a40d-44fe
    Change-Id: I9ac0e7a791c34138e42ef0df1b1d5d074df00177
    Signed-off-by: RebarBotNava <joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com>
Additionally verified in a throwaway repo BEFORE wiring: `pre-commit install` reported "Running in migration mode with existing hooks at .git/hooks/commit-msg.legacy"; a conforming commit received the legacy hook's appended Change-Id; an over-long body was rejected and `git rev-list --count HEAD` stayed at 1 (no commit created).

AC carve-outs NOT flagged: covered by tests — trailers, TAG= lines, fenced code (incl. the fence-TOGGLE case where prose after a closing fence IS still checked), 4-space/tab indented blocks, table rows, long URLs/paths.
AC detection rules match the implementation exactly (verified rule-by-rule against the code):
    trailer ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9-]*:\s | tag ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*= | fence ^\s*``` | atomic ://|[/\\]|\w[._-]\w
    indent threshold: 3 spaces -> checked, 4 spaces -> exempt, tab -> exempt (test_indent_threshold_is_four_spaces)
    a 73+ char run of ordinary characters is NOT atomic (test_long_run_of_ordinary_chars_is_not_atomic)
AC git scaffolding no false positives: comment lines and the `--verbose` diff below the `>8` marker are ignored (two tests).
AC check-only: the checker only reads the message file and prints; no write path exists.
AC `default_install_hook_types` present: line 20 of .pre-commit-config.yaml; proven effective because bare `pre-commit install` (via `make hooks`, no --hook-type flag) created the commit-msg hook.
AC `make hooks` EXITS NON-ZERO when a hook file is absent: verified — with commit-msg removed, the target takes the ERROR branch (exit 1).
AC `make hooks` WARNS but exits 0 when no Change-Id found: verified in a clean repo with no Gerrit hook — printed the WARNING plus reinstall instructions, `echo $?` = 0.
AC CONTRIBUTING.md documents it: extends the §2a note landed earlier by 368a.
AC tests: 20 passed.

GATES
Full unit suite: 5585 passed, 19 skipped. make lint clean; make typecheck "Success: no issues found in 381 source files".
Gerrit 1004 pushed with ZERO commit-message warnings, vs the `subject >50` + `too many message lines longer than 72` warnings emitted on changes 982/993/994 earlier in this session — direct evidence the gate removes the warnings at source.

RESEARCH BASIS (why 72, and why not "avoid the breaks")
Go: "wrapped at around 72 columns" + "Don't use HTML, Markdown, or any other markup language." Chromium: "wrapped to 72 columns for easier log message viewing in terminals." ChromiumOS: "Wrap the body text to 72 characters so that `git log` looks nice." Android: "hard-wraps at 72 characters maximum." No major Gerrit project solves choppy descriptions by removing line breaks; all four mandate wrapping.

SCOPE / KNOWN LIMITS (disclosed, not hidden)
- Local guardrail only, bypassable with `git commit --no-verify`; CI does NOT check wrapping (the operator explicitly chose pre-commit over CI).
- Existing history is untouched: 35 of the last 40 commits on main would fail this rule. The gate applies to new commits only.
- `make hooks` installs into the SHARED git common dir, so running it from a worktree activates the gate for the whole checkout (non-destructively — Change-Id chain verified intact).
- The plan-review gate took four rounds; all three blocking rounds were defects in the TICKET's specificity (missing `## Acceptance Criteria` shape, an ambiguous "failing/warning" outcome, then under-specified carve-out detection rules), not in the code. Fixing the third round's finding is what produced the exact regexes and the 4-space threshold now recorded above, plus two new boundary tests.
